mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) over the past two months indicates inflationary pressure, which typically leads to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (GDPC1) over the past quarter signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where GDPC1 decreases > 1% QoQ.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the past month suggests a weakening labor market, which typically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where UNRATE increases > 0.2pp MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% for three consecutive months signals an accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below 1% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the past two months indicates a strengthening demand in the housing market, which typically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where HOUST increases > 5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in Industrial Production (INDPRO) over the past two months signals a weakening supply side of the economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where INDPRO decreases > 1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) both increase over the past month, it signals a weakening labor market, which typically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE and PAYEMS both increase > 0.2pp and 0.5% MoM respectively
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where both UNRATE and PAYEMS increase as specified.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% MoM, it suggests a tightening monetary policy in response to inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where both FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% MoM.
